title: Import only from your own or a lower design-system layer

facts.note: File lies under a design root (directory named design, design_system or design-system); a repository with no design root is never judged. Excludes *.test.*, *.spec.* and vendored/build directories.
Layer is the first directory beneath the design root; derivable from the path. Files directly under the root (no named layer) are not layered.

values: file contains an import that resolves into the design system
facts.note: Import resolver mapping relative and aliased specifiers (alias naming the design directory) to a target layer. Applies to every import of a scoped file, existing or new.

fires: A file under design/primitives/ imports from design/components/ (whether the import is new or pre-existing).
A file under design-system/components/ imports from design-system/templates/ via an alias such as `@/design/templates/...`.
A tokens or foundations file imports from primitives.
doesNotFire: The repository has no directory named design, design_system or design-system.
A component imports another component in the same layer.
A component imports a primitive or a token (downward edge).
The importing file is a test file (*.test.*, *.spec.*) or lives in a vendored/build directory.
The file sits directly under the design root, outside any named layer.

given: a file inside a named layer of a design root (tokens/foundations 0, primitives 1, components 2, templates 3)
when: any of its imports resolves (relative path or alias naming the design directory) into the design system
then: each such import MUST target the file's own layer or a lower one; upward edges (tokens→primitives, primitives→components, components→templates) are forbidden
prefer: Keep imports same-layer or downward: tokens -> foundations -> primitives -> components -> templates.
Reuse an existing lower-layer value or component when possible.
Move a genuinely shared piece only to the lowest layer that actually owns it.
Compose upward rather than importing upward.
avoid: Creating a new layer or generic abstraction for one dependency.
Hiding an upward dependency behind a barrel.
unless: Imports within the same layer are allowed.
Files directly under the design root, outside any named layer, are not layered.
Test files (*.test.*, *.spec.*) and vendored/build directories are never scanned.
No design root: not judged; there is no system to connect to yet.
why: A hierarchy is only a hierarchy if dependencies flow one way; a primitive that imports a component can't be reused without dragging it along, and the layers collapse into one tangle.
evidence: The current behavioral or rendering acceptance passes.
All affected design-system imports follow the declared direction (bun_design_system_detector reports no upward edge).
verifier_detail: Design root = a directory named `design`, `design_system`, or `design-system`; the first directory beneath it names the layer: `tokens` or `foundations` (0), `primitives` (1), `components` (2), `templates` (3).

Resolve each import of a design-system file to its target layer, from a relative path or from an aliased specifier that names the design directory (e.g. `@/design/components/Card`); flag any edge whose target layer is higher than the source layer (finding = upward_import). The finding is the evaluation output, not an activation precondition.
Same-layer edges pass; files directly under the design root (no named layer) are not layered; skip `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*` and vendored/build directories; no design root => not judged (self-scoping).
Note: the statement ranks tokens and foundations together at level 0, while the fix hint lists tokens -> foundations as consecutive steps; the detector uses the statement's numbering.
Detector coverage limitation (from graph.json, not the source rule): the Bun detector inspects .tsx/.jsx/.html/.css files; this does not narrow the rule's applicability to other layered files.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.2.0.
Bun realization of the core obligation `coder.design.hierarchy-import`, mirroring `coder.vite.design-dependency-flow`.
